top_choice_rationale: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a prediction (flat bands at the magic angle) followed by an experiment in exactly that regime, with correlated insulating and superconducting states reproduced by independent groups using transport and scanning probes. A citation limited to the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated states does not depend on the unsettled pairing mechanism, and it created a tunable platform for strong correlations. Maturity and the credit left out under a three-name cap (Cao, Fatemi, Dean, Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) are real weaknesses, so the optical lattice clock (P001), with cleaner two-name attribution and longer independent confirmation, is a close second. The topological insulator part (P004) follows; the IceCube single-name pairing (P002) ranks last among awards because one name for a collaboration is hard to defend, and no award is last.
recusal_note: No direct conflict with the credited names of P003. For P001 (Katori) my University of Tokyo fellowship and long-running exchanges with Japanese universities are a possible connection, with no documented collaboration; not disqualifying. Goran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, but no proposal credits a Chalmers person.
